answer: BLS aggregate signatures let many signers compress their signatures into one short pairing-based signature over the same message, so a verifier checks a single aggregate instead of hundreds of separate ones. Each signer holds a distinct secret key bound to a public key, and the aggregate only verifies when every claimed key actually signed, like a relic sealed by many hands on one voyage across a ridge. A Sybil farm gains nothing by spawning identities, because each fake key must still produce a valid pairing signature, and forging one without its secret key is infeasible.
